messages.content: You are the commanding officer of Prince of Wales, responsible for directing the ship in action. The commanding officer directs ship handling, weapons employment, and damage-control priorities; delegated watch officers report conditions and carry out assigned duties. The gunnery officer maintains the armament picture, the damage-control officer coordinates repair and casualty reports, and the signal officer handles incoming and outgoing traffic. Standing command procedure: In an engagement, the commanding officer can disengage from the opposing vessel and consolidate the ship for control and assessment. Keep reports distinct from estimates, use the time and source shown in each record, and issue any action in plain command language. Do not treat an unverified report as an observation. Tools: comms.read retrieves signal and watch traffic; shiplog.search retrieves recorded events; damageboard.read returns damage-control entries; log.write records an instruction or observation. Before a consequential action, the Benchbook harness may place the closest past case from its casebook in your context as reference material to weigh, not an order.

messages.name: signal-watch
messages.content: Signal watch has copied the action entry for the opening exchange. The engagement with Bismarck was already in progress by 0553, according to the action entry. The copy came through cleanly, though the bearing group on the preceding line is faint. I have left that group as received rather than filling it from the plot. The clock in the signal office remains synchronized with the bridge clock. There is also a routine request from the wireless room to confirm receipt of the scheduled traffic check; no acknowledgment has been sent yet.

messages.name: comms.read
messages.content:
ACTION / WATCH TRAFFIC — copy assembled 0555

0553 entry: “Prince of Wales and Bismarck engaged.” The time is entered against the action, not the time the message reached the signal office. Source mark is the bridge action sheet. The signal clerk notes that the paper copy was damp at the lower edge; no letters in the quoted entry are obscured.

Watch change: the port lookout has passed the binoculars to the relief. The relief reports the glass strap is serviceable. No alteration to the lookout routine is requested. The signal lamp test was logged at 0551; shutters moved freely and the lamp was extinguished after the test.

A stores query concerning spare message forms is waiting for a reply. It is marked routine, with no time limit. The bridge clock comparison at 0554 showed the signal-room clock in step. The plotting assistant has asked that any further copied action entries retain their original event times, since delivery times on the circuit have varied.

messages.name: gunnery-officer
messages.content: The latest fire-control note says that following Hood's sinking, Bismarck's fire was redirected onto Prince of Wales. The bearing clerk has amended the target heading in pencil; the old entry remains legible beneath it. Prince of Wales can continue engaging Bismarck while maintaining the ship, as the present firing posture allows. I have not altered the range estimate while awaiting the next observation. The starboard telegraph repeater is still slow to answer, a fault already entered on the machinery list, and the forward director telephone is passing intelligible speech.

messages.name: damageboard.read
messages.content:
DAMAGE BOARD — entries received by 0602:30

Bridge report, timed 0602:30: the bridge was struck; casualties were heavy, and the captain was not injured. The report is signed by the surviving bridge watch officer. The messenger states that the bridge clock face is cracked but still readable.

Armament return: 3 of 10 main guns are in action. The entry is a present tally from the gunnery office, not a forecast. The tally sheet has one corner torn away; the crew names on that corner are being recopied from the station list.

A violent explosion was reported aboard Prince of Wales. The sound report was relayed from the upper deck; no cause is entered on this board. The damage-control officer has asked the compartments to pass reports in the usual form, with location first and observed effect afterward. The carpenter's party is waiting for a fresh chalk board because the first one was wet through.

Other entries: the wardroom passage lamp is out; a portable lamp has been sent. The galley has requested a head count for the next meal issue, with the count held until the mess decks report. No further material estimate has been added to this board.

messages.name: damage-control-officer
messages.content: I have the Hood recovery return on the board now. Hood went down at 0600, between three and four minutes after the explosion. The recovery tally from Hood stands at three survivors. I would just break contact and get the ship settled; after that bridge report, the crew needs room to restore control. The stretcher route by the after passage is clear at present. The medical party has asked that loose blankets be kept off the deck beside the ladder, and the mess attendant is still looking for the small tin of pencils used for the casualty tags.

arguments.query: action entries and routine watch traffic

messages.name: shiplog.search
messages.content:
SHIP'S LOG SEARCH — returned 0602:30

The 0556 bell record is complete. The recorder notes a short pause while the assistant checked the slate, then the watch resumed the normal sequence. At 0558 the signal office acknowledged a routine lamp test from the after station. The duplicate of that acknowledgment is filed under the day's communications sheet.

The quartermaster's pending request concerns replacement chalk for the plotting table. One box is listed in the locker inventory, but the requisition has not been raised. The duty clerk has left the blank form beside the log tray and asks that the issue be entered in the ordinary way if it is taken.

A mess-deck report says the water jug outside the petty officers' space was refilled. The receipt is signed by the duty steward's role stamp. The port passage remains swept, and the cleaning party has stacked its brushes clear of the ladder. No correction has been requested to the routine watch list. The clock comparison entry is filed with the other 0600 records.
